title: It didn’t come the way you expected.
paragraphs: It didn’t come the way you expected.
You thought it was another attack. Another person getting on your nerves. Another conversation that drained you, another situation that felt unfair, unnecessary… targeted.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
Not everything that opposes you is sent to destroy you. Some things are sent to reveal you.
You called it conflict. God called it an assignment.
And you felt it the moment it happened, didn’t you?

That tightening in your chest.
That quick defensive thought.
That urge to shut down, lash out, or walk away.
God saw it.
You knew.
Because it wasn’t just about them. It was touching something deeper in you—something you’ve been avoiding, something you’ve been protecting, something you didn’t want exposed.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior.
The truth is, some people enter your life not to harm you, but to confront what comfort has been hiding.

That difficult coworker.
That disrespectful family member.
That person who doesn’t respond the way you think they should.
They’re not random.
Jesus never promised you a life free from friction. In fact, He said the opposite:
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.” — Luke 9:23
Daily.
Not occasionally. Not when it’s convenient. Daily.

And sometimes that “cross” looks like loving someone who is hard to love.
Sometimes it looks like staying patient when everything in you wants to react.
Sometimes it looks like being quiet when your pride demands a response.
You said, “They disrespected me.”
But heaven is asking, “Why did it shake you so much?”
Because that’s where the assignment is.
Not in fixing them.
In transforming you.
“Count it all joy, my brothers, when you meet trials of various kinds, for you know that the testing of your faith produces steadfastness.” — James 1:2–3
Read that again.

Not avoid it.
Not escape it.
Count it joy.
Why?

Because the moment you’re most irritated…
Most triggered…
Most uncomfortable…
That’s the moment your faith is being refined.
That’s the moment God is doing something deeper than surface peace. He’s cutting into the roots—pride, control, unforgiveness, insecurity.
And you felt that resistance, didn’t you?
You wanted them to change.
But God is looking at you.
You prayed for growth.
This is how it comes.
You asked for patience.
Now someone is testing it.
You asked to be more like Christ.
And Christ… was mocked, rejected, misunderstood—and still chose love.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
He didn’t wait for people to treat Him right.
He responded from who He was, not how He was treated.
That’s the assignment.

To stop reacting from your wounds…
And start responding from your identity in Christ.
But here’s the tension no one likes to admit:

You can avoid the person…
You can leave the situation…
You can convince yourself you’re protecting your peace…
But the assignment doesn’t disappear.
It just shows up again—in a different face, a different place, the same lesson.
Because God isn’t trying to trap you.
He’s trying to transform you.
And transformation doesn’t happen in comfort.
It happens in confrontation.
“Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” — Romans 12:21
That’s not weakness.
That’s warfare.
Spiritual warfare isn’t always casting out demons.

Sometimes it’s choosing humility when your ego is screaming.
Sometimes it’s forgiving when revenge feels justified.
Sometimes it’s staying when running feels easier.
That’s where the real battle is.
And you’re in it.
So now the question isn’t, “Why are they like this?”
The real question is…
What is God trying to change in you through them?
Because one path keeps you stuck—offended, reactive, unchanged.
The other path stretches you—convicts you, refines you, reshapes you into something that actually looks like Jesus.
You already feel which one you’ve been choosing.
And you know where it’s leading.
Say it plainly: “God, show me what You’re trying to teach me.”
Not them.
You.
Follow this journey if you’re ready to stop reacting and start transforming, because the truth will keep confronting you until it sets you free.
And if you want to go deeper—to be corrected, sharpened, and built in real faith, not surface belief—step into what’s waiting for you:
This isn’t about comfort anymore.
It’s about becoming who Christ died for you to be.
